title: Case 1: which solar settings should we use?
points: Use solar generation while keeping voltage and line current within the allowed range.
An agent can organize the trials and return checked options.
note: Start with the physical problem: choose solar controls that respect voltage, current and equipment capacity while serving the stated generation goal. The agent can organize trials and return a checked option. It does not replace the solver or the operator.
caption: Concept sketch: choose settings, then calculate their effects.

title: Two tools suggest different settings
points: MPC plans with a model. SAC uses a previously trained controller.
Treat both outputs as proposals that need the same electrical checks.
note: MPC means model predictive control: it plans with a model. SAC means soft actor-critic: it uses a previously trained policy. Both produce proposals. Apply the same electrical checks to each before comparing cost or usefulness.
caption: MPC: model predictive control. SAC: soft actor-critic. Both proposals need the same checks.

title: How the agent helps with solar settings
points: The agent requests a study and reads the returned checks.
It can try another allowed option or ask the operator for help.
note: Read the loop from left to right. The operator supplies a goal. The agent requests an allowed trial. The tool calculates voltage and current. The checks decide whether it can be compared. A failed trial can lead to another permitted request or a request for help.
caption: The agent uses returned checks to choose the next permitted step.

title: Two solar settings change the result
points: One setting controls solar power output. The other provides voltage support.
The tool checks voltage, line current and the solar unit’s capacity.
note: The two controls are active-power output and voltage support. The source model represents them as a and b. They share inverter capacity, so reducing one effect can change another. Use the tool to calculate those effects rather than infer safety from the control names.
caption: Active power and voltage support share equipment capacity.

title: Both proposals face the same checks
points: The tool calculates the effect of each proposal.
Compare their scores only after voltage, current and capacity checks pass.
note: The same checks apply to both candidates. Check voltage, line current and inverter capacity first. Only a passing proposal is eligible for cost comparison. The agent’s next request should be based on the returned checks.
caption: Both proposals need the same voltage, current and capacity checks.

title: Read the voltage and current checks
points: Left: voltages should stay in the allowed band.
Right: current should stay below 100% of the allowance.
note: The left plot shows the voltage distribution. The right compares current use with the allowed current. Both pass this model’s checks. The curves on the left are sorted separately, so their horizontal rank is not a matched physical location.
caption: Calculated example at the original current allowance.

title: Both pass, but the trade-off is different
points: MPC uses 73.62% of the current allowance; SAC uses 51.68%.
MPC has the lower overall score because current is only one part of the goal.
note: The current-use values are 73.62% for MPC and 51.68% for saved SAC. Their scores are approximately 0.03110 and 0.43643. Lower score is preferred after all checks pass. SAC uses less current here partly because it also uses less active power.
caption: Calculated example: both electrical checks pass.

title: What if we allow less current?
points: Reduce the allowance from 80% to 75% of nominal current.
Which proposal might fail? Which would you choose if both pass?
What must the agent ask the tool to check again?
note: Ask people to predict without doing any calculation. Make the rule change explicit: allowed current decreases from 80% to 75% of nominal. Give pairs time to explain what must be checked again and why the lowest current is not automatically the best proposal. Advance only after the discussion.
caption: Discuss the scenario, then advance to the calculated result.

title: Both proposals pass the new current check
points: MPC has the lower score. SAC uses less current and less solar output.
These results cover the medium-voltage model. A wider grid needs a wider study.
note: The numerical study has already been calculated for this changed allowance. MPC uses about 78.53% of the new allowance and SAC about 54.85%; both pass. Their scores are about 0.03110 and 0.43246. MPC has the lower score. These checks cover the medium-voltage model, not the entire distribution system.
caption: Same load; the allowed current has been reduced to 75% of nominal.
answer_for: What if we allow less current?

title: Less current does not mean the best option
points: Here SAC also uses less solar output.
The operator’s goal values solar generation as well as operating limits.
note: In the changed-allowance example, the active-power setting is about 96% of inverter rating for MPC and 34% for SAC. These percentages use inverter rating as the base. Less current comes with a generation trade-off, so the operator’s objective matters.
caption: Active-power settings use inverter rating as their base.

title: A PASS covers only the checked model
points: A study of the medium-voltage network cannot confirm a whole-grid claim.
The agent should request the missing study or return HOLD.
note: The model’s scope travels with its result. A passing medium-voltage study does not establish low-voltage or whole-feeder safety. When the request is wider than the evidence, the useful response is a missing-study request or HOLD.
caption: A passing result applies to the model and conditions actually checked.

title: Recorded example: the first option fails
points: Llama requests a check of the saved SAC proposal.
The numerical tool reports too much current and rejects it.
note: This is a separate recorded full-feeder study, with different inputs from the earlier numerical comparison. Read the actual Llama request and returned tool result. The SAC trial reaches about 111.97% of allowed current, so it fails. The tool result determines eligibility.
caption: Recorded full-feeder study; different inputs from the earlier comparison.

title: Recorded example: another option is checked
points: Llama requests a check of the existing MPC fallback.
The returned electrical checks pass for this recorded case.
note: The agent requests a check of an existing MPC fallback. It does not invent or solve MPC. The historical electrical check returns about 99.60% of allowed current and no listed violations. That makes the option eligible for review within this study’s stated scope.
caption: Recorded full-feeder study: the requested fallback passes the checks.

title: Recorded example: the operator receives a proposal
points: The agent returns the checked proposal and its conditions.
The operator still reviews it before any authorized action.
note: The recorded workflow returns the checked proposal, while human acknowledgement remains pending and no equipment command is sent. Ask what evidence the operator receives and what remains outside the study, including permissions and protection checks.
caption: Recorded workflow result; human review remains pending.
